subject: Biotechnology
title: Carbon Capture Crops
description: A quick win: understand Carbon Capture Crops.

hook.text: What if crops stored more carbon underground? Engineering deeper roots and suberin could turn farms into carbon sinks.

buildup.text: Suberin is a waxy polymer that resists decomposition — roots coated in suberin lock carbon in soil for centuries.

discovery.text: The Salk Institute's Ideal Plants produce more suberin in deeper roots — sequestering carbon with every harvest cycle.

twist.text: Perennial grain crops maintain root systems year-round — no tilling means soil carbon stays undisturbed.

climax.text: If 50% of cropland adopted enhanced carbon-capture crops, it could offset 20% of annual CO2 emissions.

punchline.text: Grow food, bury carbon — climate-smart crops fight warming from the ground up.

quiz.question: How does suberin help crops capture carbon?
options: It absorbs CO2 from the atmosphere through the leaves
It coats roots with a decomposition-resistant polymer that locks carbon in soil for centuries
It converts carbon dioxide into oxygen more efficiently
